concepts.label: flux-vertex
concepts.gloss: A flux-vertex is a network node or site within a particular flux-fabric tier where spans terminate, switching fabric and terminations are colocated and which is a constituent part of the overall flux-fabric topology.
concepts.example: R1 is a flux-vertex in the zeta tier network that hosts terminations such as cp-A1-R1 and participates in spans like fluxspan-R1-R2 and fluxspan-A1-R1.

concepts.label: cap-point
concepts.gloss: A cap-point is a termination point located on a flux-vertex that serves as the endpoint of a flux-span and provides the attachment or 'cap' where a span is terminated at that vertex.
concepts.example: cp-R1-R2 is a cap-point on vertex R1 that terminates the link fluxspan-R1-R2 and provides the local attachment for that span at R1.

concepts.label: backing-cp
concepts.gloss: A backing-cp is an adaptation or supporting termination that implements or underpins a higher-layer cap-point (e.g., mapping a logical zeta-layer cap to an underlying optical termination) at a vertex.
concepts.example: "zeta cp over optical cp at R1" is a backing-cp that indicates the zeta-layer cap-point at R1 is supported by an underlying optical termination on the same vertex.
instances: zeta cp over optical cp at R1

concepts.label: conduit-cap-point
concepts.gloss: A conduit-cap-point (ccp) is the conduit-side termination located on a flux-vertex that serves as the origin or head for a flux-conduit service running over the fabric.
concepts.example: ccp-A1 (conduit head) is a conduit-cap-point at vertex A1 from which the conduit service conduit-a1a3-grd2 originates.

concepts.label: flux-conduit
concepts.gloss: A flux-conduit is a service-level conduit or reserved channel that runs over the flux-fabric between conduit-cap-points and represents an allocated path for carriage over the topology.
concepts.example: conduit-a1a3-grd2 (grd2, A1 to A3) is a flux-conduit that runs from ccp-A1 to ccp-A3 over the zeta tier network.

concepts.label: zeta-label
concepts.gloss: A zeta-label is a multiplexing label or carrier-slot identifier that names a specific sub-channel or slot (e.g., an xs/xpn) assigned to and labelling a flux-conduit within the carriage fabric.
concepts.example: "xs/xpn for grd2 in crr4" is a zeta-label that identifies the carrier slot used by the conduit-a1a3-grd2 within carriage-grid crr4.

concepts.label: carriage-grid
concepts.gloss: A carriage-grid is the switching or cross-connect fabric located at a flux-vertex that provides mapping and switching of labelled carrier slots and conduit endpoints on that vertex.
concepts.example: R2 carriage grid is the switching matrix at vertex R2 that performs cross-connections for zeta-labels and conduit endpoints present at R2.

concepts.label: flux-span
concepts.gloss: A flux-span is a point-to-point link between two flux-vertices within the fabric that can carry conduits and is terminated at each end by cap-points on those vertices.
concepts.example: fluxspan-R1-R2 is a flux-span connecting vertices R1 and R2 and is terminated at R1 by cp-R1-R2 and at the far end by the corresponding cap-point on R2.

concepts.label: flux-fabric
concepts.gloss: A flux-fabric is the per-tier network topology that contains the set of flux-vertices and flux-spans (the physical and logical links) over which conduits, labels and switching operate.
concepts.example: the zeta tier network is a flux-fabric that contains vertices R1, R2, R3 and spans such as fluxspan-R1-R2 and fluxspan-R2-R3 used by conduits like conduit-a1a3-grd2.

concepts.label: conduit-circuit-endpoint
concepts.gloss: A conduit-circuit-endpoint is the circuit-level endpoint representation at a flux-vertex that is part of a flux-conduit service and represents where a circuit carried in the conduit terminates on that vertex.
concepts.example: ccx-a1a3-R1 is a conduit-circuit-endpoint at vertex R1 that is part of the conduit-a1a3-grd2 service, representing the circuit termination used by equipment at R1.
